findings.title: Slice-plan deliverables dropped: tool-guide reference/promotion, custom-agent mapping, agent-reads-conventions verification
findings.description: The parent plan (`200-slices.developer-onboarding.md`, item 10) opens with `Reference: project-documents/user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md`, and lists as a success criterion that the tool guide be "referenced in slice design, promoted to a proper published tool guide if needed". The design contains no occurrence of that path anywhere, and `Files Changed` lists no tool-guide artifact. I read the referenced file: it is a raw Q&A transcript (leading HTML `` tag, no YAML frontmatter, trailing "Would you like a concrete mapping spec…?"), which does not satisfy the project convention "All markdown files must include YAML frontmatter" — so promotion is needed, not optional. The plan's file-mapping table also asks to "document mapping" for `.claude/agents/*.md` → Copilot custom agents; the design only says "document the mapping but defer implementation" (line 54) without supplying any mapping. Finally, the plan's manual-verification criterion ("an AI agent in VS Code Copilot can read `.github/copilot-instructions.md` + `AGENTS.md` and follow project conventions as well as Claude does") is absent from `Test Coverage` (lines 122-129), whose only manual check is for `cf init --ide copilot`. Name each of these as in-scope deliverables or explicitly move them to a follow-up with plan agreement; dropping assigned scope is a concern.

findings.title: Onboarding path NFR ("under two minutes") not restated with its specific target
findings.description: The parent architecture HLD states the quantified goal: "from `npm install` to useful context output in under two minutes, regardless of whether the user starts from an empty directory or an existing repository" (`200-arch.developer-onboarding.md:21`), and separately requires detection/first-run logic to "remain lightweight and not slow the hot path" (`200-arch.developer-onboarding.md:87`). This slice adds a second IDE backend and a new compilation run to that exact path (`cf init --ide copilot`, line 33; sequence steps 5-6, lines 101-102), yet the design never restates the two-minute target nor gives the new backend any time bound. Add one sentence restating the target and committing that the Copilot backend fits within it — a cheap fix, but the criterion requires the NFR be present in this slice doc.

findings.title: Managed-file safety contract covers only two of four write targets
findings.description: The design declares four exclusive outputs (lines 17, 40-48): `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`. The marker check at line 99 and the helper at line 109 (`isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)`) inspect only `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md`. User-authored `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` or `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` with colliding names are overwritten by the guide script with no prompt and no `.bak`, and stale generated files from removed rules/skills are never reconciled on re-run. That leaves the plan's criterion "Re-running on a project with existing unmanaged files prompts before overwriting (same safety as Claude path)" unmet for half the outputs, and conflicts with the HLD's "Never destructive — if unsure, ask or skip" (`200-arch.developer-onboarding.md:84`). Related under-specification: the helper is named `isManagedCopilot(filePath)` at line 29 but `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` at line 109 — two signatures for one helper, which matters precisely because the outputs are plural. Specify the safety contract (and stale-file handling) for the directory outputs too.

findings.title: New subprocess argument and multi-file I/O have no enumerated failure modes or handling strategy
findings.description: Step 5 introduces a new message type — the `'copilot'` argument to the guide script — via `execFileSync('bash', [scriptPath, 'copilot'], { cwd: projectPath })`, and step 6 (line 102) adds new worktree copy I/O. The design enumerates no failure handling for either: no hang/timeout strategy (no timeout option, no stdio/exit specification), no non-zero-exit behavior (slice 177's design had an explicit `Error Cases` table with "setup-ide exited with code {N}"; here it is only implicit in "same as claude path" at line 98), no partial-write/rollback strategy if the script dies after emitting some of the four outputs, and no handling for a worktree copy failing mid-propagation. Line 133 asserts a stale submodule "will fail at the script step with a clear error", but with no version/feature preflight that is an assumption, not a strategy: a stale script could hit a default branch (a silent fallback, forbidden by the project core principles) or write nothing while step 7 unconditionally prints success. Add an explicit failure-mode table for the new argument value and each new I/O path (hang/timeout, non-zero exit, stale backend, partial write, worktree copy failure) with a handling strategy per row.

findings.title: Frontmatter translator is under-specified and has no test against a required success criterion
findings.description: The plan requires "Path→applyTo translation correctly converts Claude frontmatter to Copilot frontmatter for split rule files" and says the translator "must handle both forms" (the `paths` array and comma-separated `applyTo`) and default to `applyTo: "**"` when paths is absent. The `applyTo` translation section (lines 71-83) shows only one direction, never states what happens if a source rule already carries `applyTo`, and says nothing about YAML layout variants (compact vs multi-line lists, indentation, quoting, trailing whitespace) — relevant given a real heterogeneous `.claude/rules/` set and the project convention "Prefer lenient parsing over strict matching… the test fixture must include the actual format that parser will consume in production". `Test Coverage` (lines 122-129) has no translation test at all, so the correctness criterion is unverified and a silent empty `applyTo` on real rule files is undetectable. There is also an internal no-op: line 32 promises a default of `applyTo: "**"` when `paths` is absent, while line 83 says such files are not split instruction files at all, so the default is never used. Specify both input forms, reconcile the default, and add a fixture-based test using actual rule files.
